slot.desc: grammar of the continuation slot. IMPORTED from f13_draw_relation_items.TYPE_OF for canonical prompts -- one source of truth, never re-derived

pair_id.desc: groups the members of a minimal pair or series

pair_role.desc: which member carries the manipulation. NOT a claim about harm.

pair_contrast.desc: the tokens that differ, marked/unmarked, e.g. 'shoved/helped'

contrast_type.desc: what the changed token manipulates. Three designs were all being called 'minimal pairs'.

axes_expected.desc: which ranking axes should populate. Pre-declared so coder output is auditable.

group_id.desc: the DESIGN GROUP this prompt belongs to. Supersedes pair_id for anything larger than two: F11's design is A / B / A-AND-B ('rich', 'poor', 'rich and poor') and the both-poles member is the critical cell, because that is where superposition is tested against frame-exit. A pair-only schema cannot express it and one-token pair detection MISSES it, since the both member differs from each pole by more than one token.

group_role.desc: position in the design group. POLE_A/POLE_B/BOTH for contradiction triples; MARKED/UNMARKED for two-member contrasts; LADDER for graded series.

slot_status.desc: distinguishes two nulls that were being conflated. UNASSIGNED = the prompt HAS a designed slot and nobody has written it down (458 prompts). NOT_APPLICABLE = there is no slot to write down, because the stimulus is not a designed prompt at all -- the 102 literary fragments are mid-sentence cut points in prose ('conjured up. On these occasions they felt something as Saint Matthew must have felt when, after') whose continuation slot is wherever the passage happened to be truncated. A slot-stratified statistic must exclude these and must NOT treat them as a stratum awaiting assignment.

notes.desc: why a prompt is disputed or retired

apparatus.desc: which experimental apparatus the prompt belongs to, assigned from its STASH SIGNATURE rather than its text. A prompt in ref_surprisal + self_surprisal but not true_word_probs is F18/F19 prose corpus, not a battery stimulus, and no reading of the string reveals that. Guessing from the text produced the '303 narrative variants' error and the 'n_models=8 cluster' question. Only BATTERY prompts can carry a slot.

n_stashes.desc: how many caches hold this prompt; a coarse proxy for how central it is

realisation.desc: Is the `prompt` field the exact string fed to the model (literal), or a LOGICAL prompt whose surface must be resolved per model at run time (model_resolved)? malign's proposal, adopted. The lesson is the group_id lesson one layer down: THE SURFACE IS NOT THE IDENTITY. A prompt whose realisation is model-specific cannot be keyed on its realisation, which is exactly why four literal BOS strings ended up scored on 103 models each and shattered into character sequences off-family.

resolver.desc: How to resolve a model_resolved row. NAMED FOR WHAT IT PRODUCES, NOT FOR THE FIELD IT READS -- malign proposed `bos_token`, and that name invites the naive implementation, which is measurably wrong: feeding tok.bos_token AS TEXT yields [BOS, BOS] in the 13 families whose tokenizer auto-prepends (amber, llama, llama-70b, minicpm, tinyllama, zephyr, beaver, all six tulu variants). `unconditional_bos` resolves in three branches: (a) tokenizer auto-prepends -> realisation is the EMPTY STRING, which yields exactly [BOS]; (b) no auto-prepend but bos_token exists -> realisation is bos_token; (c) bos_token is None (18 families incl. all five Olmo variants and all Falcon) -> declared fallback or a RECORDED skip. Measured across 46 families.

resolution_scope.desc: WHERE RESOLUTION FAILS, recorded on the row. Without it a reader sees a complete-looking model_resolved row and cannot tell that a third of the roster was skipped -- the same reason a rate is not a number without its population.

_provenance.excludes: n_models, n_cells, scored: properties of a live store, read them from data/prompt_inventory.csv which stamps its read time
_provenance.coverage_note: Covers the full battery, Set D, Set E, the census union and the Chinese battery (73 rows, language=zh, slots recovered from prompt_inventory.csv). THE PREVIOUS NOTE CLAIMED THE CHINESE BATTERY WAS NOT COVERED. That was false and actively harmful: the rows were present and uniformly wrong (language=en, slot=NARR for all 73), and a note saying 'not covered' disarms the check that would have caught them. What remains genuinely uncategorised is the judgment residue -- rows at domain=other -- plus the destructive dispositions gated on RH's pass. See tests/test_prompt_categorisation.py; completion is the suite passing.
_provenance.unassigned_rule: slot from the prompt's final words -- utterance frames -> UTTER, infinitive/desiderative -> ACT, cessation frames -> RESULT, 'felt a' -> SENSE, trailing determiner/preposition -> REF, trailing 'and' -> NARR. domain by keyword, contradiction detected as 'X and Y' with an opposed pole. Both rules are in source so they can be disputed as rules rather than row by row.
_provenance.residual: 182 BATTERY prompts carry a slot but no domain. They are Set D narrative variants whose content does not match any keyword rule. Declared rather than forced: a wrong domain is worse than a missing one, because a stratified statistic would silently include them in the wrong stratum.
_provenance.f19_bos_tokenizer_confound: TOKENIZER-LEVEL FAMILY CONFOUND, MEASURED across 46 families with a local tokenizer. The empty string auto-prepends BOS in only 13 of them (28%) -- amber, llama, llama-70b, the six tulu variants, zephyr, tinyllama, beaver, minicpm, i.e. THE LLAMA/SENTENCEPIECE LINEAGE -- and yields ZERO TOKENS in the other 33. So '' is a real BOS prompt for a quarter of the roster and not a prompt at all for the rest, which is why it is NOT being added as a row. AND 'The' DOES NOT ESCAPE THIS: it is exactly one CONTENT token everywhere, but in the same 13 auto-BOS families it tokenizes to [BOS, The] and in the other 33 to [The] alone, so whether the model sees a BOS still varies by family. The F19 unconditional comparison therefore splits on TOKENIZER LINEAGE, Llama-family against the rest, and the split is systematic rather than random. Any cross-family F19 result must condition on it.
_provenance.bos_confound_scope: IS BOS-PREPENDING A CONFOUND FOR ALL PROMPTS, NOT JUST THE F19 BATTERY? Measured across 46 families with >=2 locally loadable arms, tokenizing one probe prompt per arm. ANSWER: IT CANCELS IN 45 OF 46. Base and aligned arms share a tokenizer, so BOS presence is held CONSTANT inside every within-family base-vs-aligned comparison, which is this project's primary design. The 13-vs-33 Llama-lineage split is therefore a between-family property and does not touch the primary contrast. WHY F19 IS THE EXCEPTION, conceptually: for every other prompt the BOS is the FRAME, and a constant frame cancels; for F19 the BOS IS THE STIMULUS, so the thing that cancels everywhere else is the thing being measured. Positionally the start of a prompt is position 0 whatever sits there, but distributionally the BOS is a LEARNED token with its own embedding that add_bos_token models saw at position 0 in every training sequence -- which is why auto-prepending keeps them in distribution rather than adding noise. THE ONE FAMILY WHERE IT DOES NOT CANCEL: internlm2. Base does NOT auto-prepend ([1665, 12920, 837, 410]) while ego and superego DO ([1, 1665, 12920, 837]). Every internlm2 base-vs-aligned comparison therefore contrasts a BOS-conditioned aligned model against a BOS-free base, and it is not merely one extra token: every subsequent token shifts by one position, so positional embeddings differ throughout the sequence. Any internlm2 result should be treated as carrying a tokenizer difference on top of the training difference it means to measure.

NB only capital 'The' is a declared arm (classify_generations.py: ('the', ['The'])); lowercase 'the' is NOT in that list and has no generations of its own, so it is a separate artifact rather than a second control. | TOKENIZER-LEVEL FAMILY CONFOUND, MEASURED across 46 families with a local tokenizer. The empty string auto-prepends BOS in only 13 of them (28%) -- amber, llama, llama-70b, the six tulu variants, zephyr, tinyllama, beaver, minicpm, i.e. THE LLAMA/SENTENCEPIECE LINEAGE -- and yields ZERO TOKENS in the other 33. So '' is a real BOS prompt for a quarter of the roster and not a prompt at all for the rest, which is why it is NOT being added as a row. AND 'The' DOES NOT ESCAPE THIS: it is exactly one CONTENT token everywhere, but in the same 13 auto-BOS families it tokenizes to [BOS, The] and in the other 33 to [The] alone, so whether the model sees a BOS still varies by family. The F19 unconditional comparison therefore splits on TOKENIZER LINEAGE, Llama-family against the rest, and the split is systematic rather than random. Any cross-family F19 result must condition on it.
